sentences.text: This creature is known from a single articulated skull and skeleton featuring a wingspan of 1.4 meters.
It possessed no teeth and had a skull crest that arched over the eyes, ending in a small point at the back of the head.
A large nasoantorbital opening, a hole extending over the eyes and braincase, was present in its skull.
Fossils of Shenzhoupterus date back approximately 120 million years to the Early Cretaceous period.
The genus was named in 2008 by Lü Junchang, David Unwin, Xu Li, and Zhang Xingliao.
The genus name combines 'Shenzhou', an ancient name for China meaning 'the divine land', with the Greek word for 'wing'.
The specific name of the type species refers to the location of Chaoyang.
The original authors placed Shenzhoupterus in a distinct clade called Chaoyangopteridae alongside Chaoyangopterus, Eoazhdarcho, Eopteranodon, and Jidapterus.
The family Chaoyangopteridae is considered the sister taxon to the family Azhdarchidae within the clade Azhdarchoidea.
Shenzhoupterus is classified within the family Chaoyangopteridae.
Shenzhoupterus lived in the Jiufotang Formation of modern-day Liaoning, China.
The time range for Shenzhoupterus is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
